statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail risk remains in the low band on an observed shallow drift to the lower edge of a narrow overnight band, with a flagged checkpoint window around the US cash open, the S&P Global flash PMIs and the EIA crude report.
recommendation: Conditions remain consistent with normal mean-reverting behaviour outside a narrow checkpoint window of 13:30-14:30 UTC (15:30-16:30 Berlin), when the opening auction, the flash PMIs and the EIA crude report cluster. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by this assessment.
headline: Nasdaq-100 futures drift to the lower edge of a narrow overnight band as yields firm and chips lag; Tail held low with a flagged cash-open and flash-PMI window
body: NQ futures are trading near 30,933.5, about 0.31% below the prior settle of 31,028.5 and only some 23 points above the 30,910.75 overnight low, inside a band of roughly 30,910.75-31,094.75 that spans about 0.59%. Price has worked steadily toward the lower edge of that band through the European morning, which is a shallow one-directional drift rather than a pathological path: the absolute move is small, VIX at 14.32 is only 0.11 above the prior close of 14.21, and there is no observed repeated extension after failed retracements. The index is near an overnight extreme, which is counted as a single mild amplifier rather than as confirmation of persistent one-way structure. The multi-day regime remains a bullish uptrend: the Nasdaq-100 cash index closed at 30,732.40 on 22 September, up 0.82% and at the top of its 52-week range, after Meta's Muse AI agent drove a chip-led rally to successive Nasdaq records. That prior strength is a conditional amplifier for the opening auction, not observed structure, so it is scored into the forecast rather than into current Tail. Internals are split rather than aligned, which is the main reason Tail stays low. Software is firm, with Microsoft up 0.97% and Apple up 0.34%, while semiconductors are broadly lower, led by ARM at -2.71%, Intel at -1.66% and Micron at -1.23%; Software-Infrastructure and Software-Application industry groups are positive against Semiconductor Equipment at -2.10%. Conflicting breadth of this kind reduces directional conviction and lifts Stress rather than Tail. Cross-asset evidence is modestly risk-negative: the US 10-year yield has firmed to about 4.98%, up some 3.5 basis points, with the 30-year near 5.32%, and the 2-year was 4.76% on the latest H.15 observation, so the duration channel is a live headwind for long-duration technology. Crude has stopped falling after six declining sessions, with WTI near $90.8 and Brent back above $100 at $100.47, as the Saudi East-West pipeline restart and reported US-Iran contacts at the UN are weighed against an unresolved Hormuz disruption; that keeps a floor under Stress without creating a discontinuity. Tail is therefore lifted marginally to 14 and Stress to 39. The flagged window covers the 13:30 UTC cash open, the 13:45 UTC S&P Global flash PMIs and the 14:30 UTC EIA crude report; conditional Tail peaks at 21 in the 13:00 UTC hour and 20 in the 14:00 UTC hour, then decays on the base case of orderly price discovery, with a secondary lift to 17 in the 19:00 UTC power hour. The 17:00 UTC 5-year note auction and the Trump-Xi state visit later this week are treated as checkpoints in the forecast, not as observed drivers. Shared Finviz cross-asset context was about ten minutes old but reported collection status partial, with the futures and calendar sections unavailable; its breadth, megacap and semiconductor sections were used only as latest-session confirmation of the rotation described above, and all price-path, yield, oil and volatility levels in this assessment come from independently verified primary sources.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hourly slots carry a published Claude assessment, so coverage is continuous with no gap. Tail ranged from 10 to 21, with three WATCH hours clustered around the 22 September US cash open at 14:00 UTC and the 18:00-19:00 UTC afternoon, each resolving back into the low band within one to two hours. The trend-up labelling that ran from 20:00 UTC through 01:00 UTC gave way to a normal, range-rotating mode from 02:00 UTC onward, with Tail between 10 and 12 and Stress easing from 37 to 33 before firming back to 35-36 through the European morning. Confidence held between 84 and 88 throughout.
outlookSummary: The forecast keeps Tail in the low band for 22 of 24 hours and concentrates conditional risk in one narrow window. Tail rises from 14 to 21 in the 13:00 UTC hour, which contains both the cash open and the flash PMIs, and holds at 20 in the 14:00 UTC hour alongside the EIA crude report; those two slots are the only WATCH hours. Because a record close and a chip-led rally sit behind the open, opening-auction continuation with shallow pullbacks is the specific conditional amplifier to test, and it is not observed at the assessment cutoff. On the base case of orderly price discovery Tail decays to 17 by 15:00 UTC and 14 by 18:00 UTC, with the 17:00 UTC 5-year note auction holding Stress marginally higher and a secondary Tail lift to 17 in the 19:00 UTC power hour on closing-auction imbalance. The overnight cycle returns to 10-11 with no scheduled US release, then firms to 12-13 into Thursday's 12:30 UTC jobless claims and the Trump-Xi state visit. Confidence declines gradually from 87 to 78 as distance from the verified evidence grows.
